title: 2013 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：无现金社会为何迟迟不来——四股力量拖住纸质支付。空多考搭配（work against、cope with），13 题是因果不是让步。

paras.en: Given the advantages of electronic money, you might think that we would move quickly to the cashless society in which all payments are made electronically. 1 , a true cashless society is probably not around the corner. Indeed, predictions have been 2 for two decades but have not yet come to fruition. For example, Business Week predicted in 1975 that electronic means of payment would soon "revolutionize the very 3 of money itself," only to 4 itself several years later. Why has the movement to a cashless society been so 5 in coming?
paras.zh: 鉴于电子货币的种种优点，你也许会以为我们会很快迈入无现金社会，一切支付都在电子网络上完成。1，真正的无现金社会大概不会很快到来。诚然，这类预言已经流传了二十年，却至今没有成为现实。例如，《商业周刊》1975 年曾预言，电子支付手段很快就会“彻底变革货币本身的 3”，结果几年后却 4 了自己。为什么迈向无现金社会的进程来得如此 5？

paras.en: Although electronic means of payment may be more efficient than a payments system based on paper, several factors work 6 the disappearance of the paper system. First, it is very 7 to set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications networks necessary to make electronic money the 8 form of payment. Second, paper checks have the advantage that they 9 receipts, something that many consumers are unwilling to 10 . Third, the use of paper checks gives consumers several days of "float" — it takes several days 11 a check is cashed and funds are 12 from the issuer's account, which means that the writer of the check can earn interest on the funds in the meantime. 13 electronic payments are immediate, they eliminate the float for the consumer.
paras.zh: 尽管电子支付手段可能比以纸张为基础的支付体系更有效率，却有几项因素 6 纸质体系的消失。第一，要让电子货币成为 8 的支付形式，所需的电脑、读卡器和电信网络的搭建非常 7。第二，纸质支票有一项优势：它们能 9 收据，而许多消费者不愿 10 这一点。第三，使用纸质支票能给消费者几天“浮存期”——要过几天时间 11 支票才兑现、款项才从开票人账户中 12 出来，这意味着开票人在这段时间里可以赚取这笔资金的利息。13 电子支付是即时到账的，它们让消费者失去了这段浮存期。

paras.en: Fourth, electronic means of payment may 14 security and privacy concerns. We often hear media reports that an unauthorized hacker has been able to access a computer database and to alter information 15 there. The fact that this is not an 16 occurrence means that dishonest persons might be able to access bank accounts in electronic payments systems and 17 from someone else's accounts. The 18 of this type of fraud is no easy task, and a new field of computer science is developing to 19 security issues. A further concern is that the use of electronic means of payment leaves an electronic 20 that contains a large amount of personal data. There are concerns that government, employers, and marketers might be able to access these data, thereby violating our privacy.
paras.zh: 第四，电子支付手段可能 14 安全与隐私方面的担忧。我们常听到媒体报道，有未经授权的黑客侵入计算机数据库，篡改 15 在那里的信息。这类事件并非 16，这意味着不诚实的人也许能够进入电子支付系统中的银行账户，从别人的账户里 17。18 这类诈骗绝非易事，计算机科学的一个新领域正在发展起来，以 19 安全问题。还有一层担忧是：使用电子支付手段会留下电子 20，其中包含大量个人数据。人们担心政府、雇主和营销商也许能获取这些数据，从而侵犯我们的隐私。

items.exp: 定位首段②句：上句说“你也许以为我们会很快迈入无现金社会”，本句却说“真正的无现金社会大概不会很快到来”，前后是预期与现实的转折，故选 However。Moreover 表递进、Therefore 表因果、Otherwise 表“否则”，都无法承接这种“看似如此、其实不然”的反转。
定位同句 predictions have been 2 for two decades but have not yet come to fruition：be around 意为“存在、流传”，与 but 引出的“尚未实现”正好构成对照。be off 是“取消、变质”，be back 是“回来”，be over 是“结束”，都不能与 for two decades 连用表示“流传了二十年”。
定位同句 revolutionize the very 3 of money itself：被“彻底变革”的是人们对“货币是什么”的理解，即 the concept of money（货币这一概念）。power 指权力、history 指历史、role 指角色，都无法被“电子支付”从根本上推翻，也与后文“纸质支付与电子支付的替代”这一论题不合。
定位同句 only to 4 itself several years later：only to 引出的是令人失望的意外结果——《商业周刊》的预言几年后反被自己推翻，reverse oneself 意为“自我否定、反转”。resist 是“抵制”外来的东西，resume 是“恢复、继续”，reward 是“奖励”，三者都无法与 itself 搭配成“自打嘴巴”之意。
定位首段末句 Why has the movement to a cashless society been so 5 in coming：全文要回答的正是“这个进程为何姗姗来迟”，slow in coming 是固定说法。silent 与 coming 不搭；sudden 与“二十年未实现”自相矛盾；steady 强调“平稳持续”，不含“迟”义。
定位第二段首句 several factors work 6 the disappearance of the paper system：下文列举的设备昂贵、支票可作收据、浮存期、安全隐私，都是“阻碍”纸质体系消失的因素，work against 意为“不利于、阻碍”。work for 是“有利于”，work with 是“与……合作”，work on 是“致力于”，方向全都相反。

定位第二段②句 it is very 7 to set up the computer, card reader, and telecommunications networks：铺设电脑、读卡器与电信网络是一笔巨额投入，故 expensive。imaginative（富有想象力）、sensitive（敏感的）、productive（多产的）都不能描述“建设成本”，也就无法构成“纸质体系难被取代”的第一条理由。
定位同句 necessary to make electronic money the 8 form of payment：只有成为“占主导地位的”支付形式，才需要如此庞大的基础设施，dominant 与下文“取代纸质支付”的语境一致。similar（相似的）、original（最初的）、temporary（临时的）都无法体现“取代”这一目标。
定位第二段③句 paper checks have the advantage that they 9 receipts：支票的长处在于能“提供”收据，作为交易凭证，provide 搭配成立。collect 的主语应是人（收款人收集收据）；copy（复印）、print（打印）只涉形式，不足以成为“消费者不愿放弃”的优势。
定位同句 something that many consumers are unwilling to 10：that 指代“支票能提供收据”这一便利，消费者不愿“放弃”它，give up 正确。take over（接管）、bring back（带回）、pass down（传给后代）都与“舍不得丢掉既有凭证”的心理不符。
定位第二段④句 it takes several days 11 a check is cashed：it takes + 一段时间 + before... 是固定句型，意为“要过多久才……”，强调支票兑现、款项划出之间的时间差。after 与 takes 搭配不通；since 需与完成时连用；when 只表时点，体现不出“延迟几天”。
定位同句 funds are 12 from the issuer's account：钱是从开票人账户里“被划走”的，withdraw 意为“提取、取出”，与 from 搭配。kept（保留）、borrowed（借入）方向相反；released 意为“释放、放行”，不用于资金从账户转出。
定位第二段末句 13 electronic payments are immediate, they eliminate the float for the consumer：电子支付“即时到账”正是它“消灭浮存期”的原因，前后为因果，故 Because。Unless（除非）、Until（直到）、Though（尽管）都会切断这层因果，使“浮存期消失”失去解释。
定位第三段首句 electronic means of payment may 14 security and privacy concerns：电子支付会“引起”安全与隐私担忧，raise concerns 是固定搭配。hide（掩盖）、ease（缓解）与下文黑客、诈骗的负面描述相反；express 的主语应是人，不能是支付手段。
定位第三段②句 alter information 15 there：there 指计算机数据库，黑客进去篡改的是“存储”在其中的信息，stored there 作后置定语。analyzed（分析）、shared（共享）、displayed（显示）都不能准确交代数据库里信息的常态，也无法解释“篡改”的危害。
定位第三段③句 The fact that this is not an 16 occurrence：双重否定表达“此类事件并不罕见”，才顺理成章引出“不诚实者可能入侵别人账户”的推论。unsafe、unnatural、unclear 与 occurrence 搭配后都读不出“频繁发生”之意，推论链就断了。
定位同句 access bank accounts ... and 17 from someone else's accounts：进入他人账户之后自然是“偷钱”，steal from 搭配正确，也与本段 fraud 的主题一致。choose（挑选）、return（归还）与犯罪语境不合；benefit from 虽可搭配，但意为“从……中受益”，不含非法取得之义。
定位第三段④句 The 18 of this type of fraud is no easy task：既然下一句说计算机科学的新领域正发展起来“应对安全问题”，此处应是“防范这类诈骗绝非易事”，prevention 正确。consideration（考虑）、manipulation（操纵）、justification（辩护）都无法与 no easy task 组成“治理犯罪”之意。
定位同句 a new field of computer science is developing to 19 security issues：新学科要“应对、处理”安全问题，cope with 最贴切。call for 是“需要”，主语不对；adapt to 是“适应”，含被动迁就之意；fight against 侧重“对抗打击”，与“学科处理技术难题”的搭配不如 cope with 准确。
定位第三段⑤句 leaves an electronic 20 that contains a large amount of personal data：电子支付会留下“电子痕迹”，electronic trail 是固定说法，正好接“含大量个人数据”。chunk（大块）、chip（芯片）是实体部件，不会“留下”；path 指路径，不含“数据记录”之义。

sections.title: Text 1　“平庸”时代的终结
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：自动化与全球化让“中等水平”不再能换来中产生活，出路是独特价值与教育。23 题注意 erased 的对象是“七十年就业增长”。

paras.en: In an essay entitled "Making It in America," the author Adam Davidson relates a joke from cotton country about just how much a modern textile mill has been automated: The average mill has only two employees today, "a man and a dog. The man is there to feed the dog, and the dog is there to keep the man away from the machines."
paras.zh: 在《在美国谋生》一文中，作者亚当·戴维森讲了一个来自棉花产区的笑话，用来说明现代纺织厂的自动化程度：如今一家普通纺织厂只有两名员工，“一个人和一条狗。人在那儿喂狗，狗在那儿看着人，不让他靠近机器”。

paras.en: Davidson's article is one of a number of pieces that have recently appeared making the point that the reason we have such stubbornly high unemployment and declining middle-class incomes today is largely because of the big drop in demand because of the Great Recession, but it is also because of the advances in both globalization and the information technology revolution, which are more rapidly than ever replacing labor with machines or foreign workers.
paras.zh: 戴维森的这篇文章只是近来涌现的众多同类文章之一，它们都指出：如今失业率居高不下、中产阶级收入不断下滑，很大程度上是大萧条导致需求大幅萎缩所致，但同时也源于全球化和信息技术革命的进步——这两股力量正以空前的速度用机器或外国工人取代劳动力。

paras.en: In the past, workers with average skills, doing an average job, could earn an average lifestyle. But, today, average is officially over. Being average just won't earn you what it used to. It can't when so many more employers have so much more access to so much more above average cheap foreign labor, cheap robotics, cheap software, cheap automation and cheap genius. Therefore, everyone needs to find their extra — their unique value contribution that makes them stand out in whatever is their field of employment.
paras.zh: 过去，技能平平、工作平平的劳动者也能过上中等水平的生活。但今天，“平庸”已被正式宣告终结。做个平庸之辈，再也换不来过去的所得。当越来越多的雇主能够越来越容易地获得越来越多水平中上的廉价外国劳动力、廉价机器人、廉价软件、廉价自动化和廉价天才时，平庸自然行不通了。因此，每个人都要找到自己的“加分项”——那种能让自己在本行业里脱颖而出的独特价值贡献。

paras.en: Yes, new technology has been eating jobs forever, and always will. But there's been an acceleration. As Davidson notes, "In the 10 years ending in 2009, [U.S.] factories shed workers so fast that they erased almost all the gains of the previous 70 years; roughly one out of every three manufacturing jobs — about 6 million in total — disappeared."
paras.zh: 的确，新技术一直在吞噬工作岗位，将来也会如此。但这一进程已经加速。正如戴维森所指出的：“在截至 2009 年的十年里，（美国）工厂裁减工人的速度如此之快，几乎抹掉了此前七十年积累的全部增长；大约每三个制造业岗位就有一个消失，合计约六百万个。”

paras.en: There will always be change — new jobs, new products, new services. But the one thing we know for sure is that with each advance in globalization and the I. T. revolution, the best jobs will require workers to have more and better education to make themselves above average.
paras.zh: 变化总会存在——新工作、新产品、新服务。但有一点我们完全可以确定：随着全球化和信息技术革命的每一次推进，最好的工作都将要求劳动者接受更多、更好的教育，从而让自己高于平均水平。

paras.en: In a world where average is officially over, there are many things we need to do to support employment, but nothing would be more important than passing some kind of G. I. Bill for the 21st century that ensures that every American has access to post-high school education.
paras.zh: 在一个“平庸”已被正式宣告终结的世界里，为支撑就业我们需要做很多事，但没有什么比通过一部面向 21 世纪的《退伍军人法案》式法律更重要——它要确保每个美国人都能接受高中后教育。

items.stem: The joke in Paragraph 1 is used to illustrate
items.exp: 定位首段：工厂只剩“一个人和一条狗”，人的作用只是喂狗、狗的作用是把人挡在机器之外，夸张地写出自动化程度之高；第二段随即点明技术进步（globalization and the information technology revolution）正在用机器取代人。笑话服务于“技术冲击”这一论点，故 A。C 只抓 textile mill 的字面，笑话的重点不是厂子变小；D 是第二段的话题，不是首段笑话的直接用意。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 3, to be a successful employee, one has to
items.exp: 定位第三段末句 everyone needs to find their extra — their unique value contribution that makes them stand out in whatever is their field of employment，D 的 contribute something unique 正是 unique value contribution 的同义替换。A 把“雇主可获得的廉价软件”误当成雇员该做的事；C 与同段 average is officially over 完全相反。

items.stem: The quotation in Paragraph 4 explains that
opts: gains of technology have been erased
job opportunities are disappearing at a high speed
factories are making much less money than before
new jobs and services have been offered
items.exp: 定位第四段引文：factories shed workers so fast that they erased almost all the gains of the previous 70 years，约三分之一制造业岗位消失，引文是为“岗位正在高速消失”提供证据，B 对应。A 偷换宾语——被抹掉的是“七十年的就业增长”，不是“技术收益”；C 谈利润、D 谈新岗位，都不是引文内容，D 甚至来自下一段的转折句。

items.stem: According to the author, to reduce unemployment, the most important is
opts: to accelerate the I. T. revolution
to ensure more education for people
to pass more bills in the 21st century
items.exp: 定位末段 nothing would be more important than passing some kind of G. I. Bill for the 21st century that ensures that every American has access to post-high school education，落脚点是“让更多人接受教育”，B 正确。D 把“通过一部教育法案”泛化成“通过更多法案”，属偷换；A、C 是作者认定造成岗位流失的原因，不可能同时是解药。

items.stem: Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the text?
items.exp: 定位第三段 average is officially over 与末段 In a world where average is officially over，这一说法在文中既是判断也是论证起点，最能统摄全文，故 C。A 的 New Law 只是末段一项尚待通过的建议，且“生效”无据；B 只覆盖第三段“一切都变廉价”的细节；D 把大萧条当主线，而作者明说衰退只是部分原因。

sections.title: Text 2　为“候鸟式”移民正名
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：呼吁跳出“合法／非法”的二分，接纳来去自由的“候鸟”移民。27 题“已修复”是反向陷阱，30 题标题落在“二分错了”。

paras.en: A century ago, the immigrants from across the Atlantic included settlers and sojourners. Along with the many folks looking to make a permanent home in the United States came those who had no intention to stay, and who would make some money and then go home. Between 1908 and 1915, about 7 million people arrived while about 2 million departed. About a quarter of all Italian immigrants, for example, eventually returned to Italy for good. They even had an affectionate nickname, "uccelli di passaggio," birds of passage.
paras.zh: 一个世纪以前，跨越大西洋而来的移民中既有定居者，也有旅居者。在众多希望在美国安家落户的人之外，还有一批人压根没打算久留，他们赚些钱就回国。1908 年至 1915 年间，约七百万人抵达美国，同时约二百万人离开。以意大利移民为例，约四分之一最终永久返回意大利。他们甚至有个亲昵的绰号——“uccelli di passaggio”，即“候鸟”。

paras.en: Today, we are much more rigid about immigrants. We divide newcomers into two categories: legal or illegal, good or bad. We hail them as Americans in the making, or brand them as aliens to be kicked out. That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long political paralysis over how to fix it. We don't need more categories, but we need to change the way we think about categories. We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal. To start, we can recognize the new birds of passage, those living and thriving in the gray areas. We might then begin to solve our immigration challenges.
paras.zh: 如今，我们对移民的态度要僵化得多。我们把新来者分成两类：合法或非法，好的或坏的。我们要么称赞他们是“正在成长中的美国人”，要么给他们贴上“应当驱逐的外国人”的标签。这套框架在很大程度上造就了我们漏洞百出的移民制度，也造成了长期以来在“如何修补”问题上的政治僵局。我们不需要更多分类，而需要改变对分类的思考方式。我们需要超越对“合法”与“非法”的严格界定。首先，我们可以承认这些新的“候鸟”，承认那些在灰色地带生活和兴旺的人。这样，我们或许才能着手解决移民难题。

paras.en: Crop pickers, violinists, construction workers, entrepreneurs, engineers, home health-care aides and physicists are among today's birds of passage. They are energetic participants in a global economy driven by the flow of work, money and ideas. They prefer to come and go as opportunity calls them. They can manage to have a job in one place and a family in another.
paras.zh: 今天的“候鸟”中有农作物采摘工、小提琴手、建筑工人、创业者、工程师、家庭护理员和物理学家。他们是这个由工作、资金和观念流动所驱动的全球经济中活跃的参与者。他们更愿意随着机会的召唤而来去。他们能够在一处有工作，在另一处有家庭。

paras.en: With or without permission, they straddle laws, jurisdictions and identities with ease. We need them to imagine the United States as a place where they can be productive for a while without committing themselves to staying forever. We need them to feel that home can be both here and there and that they can belong to two nations honorably.
paras.zh: 无论有没有许可，他们都游刃有余地跨越法律、司法辖区和身份归属。我们需要让他们把美国想象成一个可以暂时施展才干、而不必承诺永久居留的地方。我们需要让他们觉得，家可以既在这里又在那里，他们可以有尊严地同时属于两个国家。

paras.en: Accommodating this new world of people in motion will require new attitudes on both sides of the immigration battle. Looking beyond the culture war logic of right or wrong means opening up the middle ground and understanding that managing immigration today requires multiple paths and multiple outcomes, including some that are not easy to accomplish legally in the existing system.
paras.zh: 要容纳这个人口流动的新世界，移民之争的双方都需要新的态度。超越“非对即错”的文化战争逻辑，意味着打开中间地带，并认识到当今管理移民需要多条路径、多种结果，其中有些在现行制度下难以合法实现。

items.stem: "Birds of passage" refers to those who
opts: stay in a foreign country temporarily
leave their home countries for good
items.exp: 定位首段：sojourners 是“had no intention to stay... make some money and then go home”，意大利移民中约四分之一最终回国，故 birds of passage 指“在他国暂居的人”，A 正确。B 的 for good 是“永久离开”，恰好说反了——原文是“永久回到祖国”；C 只说了移民的路线，D 的 permanent 与“暂居”矛盾。

items.stem: It is implied in Paragraph 2 that the current immigration system in the US
opts: should be adapted to meet challenges
has been fixed via political means
items.exp: 定位第二段：That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system and the long political paralysis over how to fix it，可见现行体制失灵、亟待调整，C 正确。A 与 We don't need more categories 直接冲突；D 的 has been fixed 与 broken、paralysis 相反；B 的 loosened control 文中无据。

items.stem: According to the author, today's birds of passage want
opts: the freedom to stay and leave
items.exp: 定位第三段 They prefer to come and go as opportunity calls them，以及 They can manage to have a job in one place and a family in another，核心诉求是“来去自由”，C 的 the freedom to stay and leave 是同义替换。A 的 financial incentives、B 的 global recognition 文中均未提及；D 的 regular jobs 与“哪儿有机会就去哪儿”的流动性相反。

items.stem: The author suggests that the birds of passage today should be treated
items.exp: 定位第二段 We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal 与末段 including some that are not easy to accomplish legally in the existing system：作者主张在“合法／非法”的硬界限之外给这类人以空间，即法律上的宽容，B 正确。A、D 是对身份的定性，文中从未把他们称作伙伴或对手；C 的 economic favors 把“法律宽容”偷换成“经济优待”。

items.stem: The most appropriate title for this text would be
items.exp: 定位第二段 That framework has contributed mightily to our broken immigration system 与 We need to look beyond strict definitions of legal and illegal：全文否定的正是“合法／非法”这套二分法，D 直接点出该框架是个错误。A、B、C 都只是从文中捡了 come and go、living and thriving、with or without 等短语，再硬加上原文没有的 Big Mistake、Great Risk 之类判断。

sections.title: Text 3　快速反应可以被“暂停”扭转
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：本能式的快速判断能被“停一下”修正。31 题按“紧迫程度”分层，别选成“预先决定准确性”；34 题依据是“厚片”信息。

paras.en: Scientists have found that although we are prone to snap overreactions, if we take a moment and think about how we are likely to react, we can reduce or even eliminate the negative effects of our quick, hard-wired responses.
paras.zh: 科学家发现，尽管我们容易做出即时的过度反应，但只要花一点时间想一想自己可能会如何反应，就能减轻甚至消除这种快速、本能反应的负面影响。

paras.en: Snap decisions can be important defense mechanisms; if we are judging whether someone is dangerous, our brains and bodies are hard-wired to react very quickly, within milliseconds. But we need more time to assess other factors. To accurately tell whether someone is sociable, studies show, we need at least a minute, preferably five. It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality, like neuroticism or open-mindedness.
paras.zh: 即时判断可以是重要的防御机制：如果我们要判断某人是否有危险，大脑和身体会本能地在几毫秒内迅速反应。但要评估其他因素，我们则需要更多时间。研究表明，要准确判断一个人是否善于交际，我们至少需要一分钟，最好是五分钟。判断性格中复杂的方面，比如神经质或开放性，是需要时间的。

paras.en: But snap decisions in reaction to rapid stimuli aren't exclusive to the interpersonal realm. Psychologists at the University of Toronto found that viewing a fast-food logo for just a few milliseconds primes us to read 20 percent faster, even though reading has little to do with eating. We unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing, Subjects exposed to fast-food flashes also tend to think a musical piece lasts too long.
paras.zh: 不过，对快速刺激作出即时判断并不限于人际领域。多伦多大学的心理学家发现，只要看几毫秒快餐标志，我们的阅读速度就会提高 20%，尽管阅读与吃饭几乎无关。我们会不自觉地把快餐与速度、急躁联系起来，并把这种冲动带进手头正在做的任何事。接触过快餐标志闪现的受试者也往往觉得一段音乐持续得太久。

paras.en: Yet we can reverse such influences. If we know we will overreact to consumer products or housing options when we see a happy face (one reason good sales representatives and real estate agents are always smiling), we can take a moment before buying. If we know female job screeners are more likely to reject attractive female applicants, we can help screeners understand their biases — or hire outside screeners.
paras.zh: 不过，我们可以逆转这类影响。如果我们知道自己看到笑脸时会对消费品或房源过度反应（这也是优秀销售代表和房产经纪人总是面带微笑的原因之一），我们就可以在购买前先停一停。如果我们知道女性招聘官更可能拒绝有魅力的女性求职者，我们就可以帮助招聘官认识自己的偏见——或者聘请外部筛选人员。

paras.en: John Gottman, the marriage expert, explains that we quickly "thin slice" information reliably only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study. When Dr. Gottman really wants to assess whether a couple will stay together, he invites them to his island retreat for a much longer evaluation: two days, not two seconds.
paras.zh: 婚姻专家约翰·戈特曼解释说，只有把这类快速反应建立在“厚片式”长期研究的基础上，我们才能可靠地对信息做“薄片式”的快速判断。当戈特曼博士真的想评估一对夫妻能否走下去时，他会请他们到自己的海岛静居处做一次长得多的评估：两天，而不是两秒。

paras.en: Our ability to mute our hard-wired reactions by pausing is what differentiates us from animals: dogs can think about the future only intermittently or for a few minutes. But historically we have spent about 12 percent of our days contemplating the longer term. Although technology might change the way we react, it hasn't changed our nature. We still have the imaginative capacity to rise above temptation and reverse the high-speed trend.
paras.zh: 我们能够通过暂停来抑制本能反应，这正是人与动物的区别：狗只能断断续续地、或只用几分钟去想未来。而从历史上看，我们每天约有 12% 的时间在思考更长远的事。尽管技术可能改变我们反应的方式，却没有改变我们的天性。我们仍然拥有想象力，足以超越诱惑、扭转这种高速化的趋势。

items.stem: The time needed in making decisions may
opts: predetermine the accuracy of our judgment
prove the complexity of our brain reaction
depend on the importance of the assessment
vary according to the urgency of the situation
items.exp: 定位第二段：判断“是否有危险”只需几毫秒，判断“是否善于交际”至少要一分钟，判断复杂人格还需更久，所需时间随情形的紧迫与复杂程度而变，D 正确。A 把“时间影响准确性”放大成“预先决定准确性”；B 说“大脑反应的复杂性”，原文讲的是“人格的复杂性”；C 的 importance 原文未提，无法与三档情形对应。

items.stem: Our reaction to a fast-food logo shows that snap decisions
items.exp: 定位第三段 We unconsciously associate fast food with speed and impatience and carry those impulses into whatever else we're doing：快餐标志之所以能加快阅读，靠的是“联想”机制，A 正确。B 的 not unconscious 与 unconsciously 直接相反；C 的 dangerous 是第二段“判断危险”的语境，与本段无关；D 的 not impulsive 与同段 impulses 相悖。

items.stem: To reverse the negative influences of snap decisions, we should
items.exp: 定位第四段 Yet we can reverse such influences 之后的两个 If：知道看到笑脸会冲动，就 we can take a moment before buying，即“先想一想再行动”，B 正确。A 的 trust our first impression 恰是作者要纠正的对象；C 与“反制本能”相反；D 的专家建议只出现在“聘请外部筛选人员”这一具体细节里，被放大成通用建议。

items.stem: John Gottman says that reliable snap reactions are based on
items.exp: 定位第五段 we quickly "thin slice" information reliably only after we ground such snap reactions in "thick sliced" long-term study：可靠的前提是“厚片式”的长期研究，也就是掌握充分信息，C 正确。B 把 only after 之后的条件误当成依据，thin slice 恰是“不能只靠”的东西；A 的 critical assessment、D 的 sensible explanation 文中均无对应表述。

items.stem: The author's attitude toward reversing the high-speed trend is
items.exp: 定位末段 We still have the imaginative capacity to rise above temptation and reverse the high-speed trend：作者相信人类仍有能力扭转趋势，态度是乐观，B 正确。D 的 Doubtful 与 still have the capacity 正相反；C 的 uncertain 无视了作者的明确判断；A 的 tolerant 是“容忍”，不含“看好”之意，语气也不对。

sections.title: Text 4　欧盟的女性董事配额之争
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：自愿呼吁失败后，作者虽反感配额却认可“暂时强制”。38 题 break through 不是 see through，属形近陷阱。

paras.en: Europe is not a gender-equality heaven. In particular, the corporate workplace will never be completely family-friendly until women are part of senior management decisions, and Europe's top corporate-governance positions remain overwhelmingly male. Indeed, women hold only 14 per cent of positions on European corporate boards.
paras.zh: 欧洲并非性别平等的天堂。尤其是，除非女性参与高层管理决策，企业职场永远不会变得完全兼顾家庭；而欧洲企业最高治理职位仍以男性压倒性占据。事实上，女性在欧洲企业董事会中只占 14% 的席位。

paras.en: The European Union is now considering legislation to compel corporate boards to maintain a certain proportion of women — up to 60 per cent. This proposed mandate was born of frustration. Last year, European Commission Vice President Viviane Reding issued a call to voluntary action. Reding invited corporations to sign up for gender balance goals of 40 per cent female board membership. But her appeal was considered a failure: only 24 companies took it up.
paras.zh: 欧盟目前正在考虑立法，强制企业董事会保持一定比例的女性——最高可达 60%。这项拟议的强制要求源于无奈。去年，欧盟委员会副主席维维亚娜·雷丁发出自愿行动的呼吁。雷丁邀请企业签署性别平衡目标，让女性占董事会成员的 40%。但她的呼吁被认为失败了：只有 24 家公司响应。

paras.en: Do we need quotas to ensure that women can continue to climb the corporate ladder fairly as they balance work and family?
paras.zh: 我们是否需要配额，来确保女性在兼顾工作与家庭的同时，能够继续公平地攀登企业晋升阶梯？

paras.en: "Personally, I don't like quotas," Reding said recently. "But I like what the quotas do." Quotas get action: they "open the way to equality and they break through the glass ceiling," according to Reding, a result seen in France and other countries with legally binding provisions on placing women in top business positions.
paras.zh: “就我个人而言，我不喜欢配额，”雷丁最近说，“但我喜欢配额所起的作用。”配额能带来行动：据雷丁说，它们“打开了通往平等之路，也打破了玻璃天花板”，这一结果在法国以及其他以具有法律约束力的条款把女性送入企业高层的国家已经显现。

paras.en: I understand Reding's reluctance — and her frustration. I don't like quotas either; they run counter to my belief in meritocracy, governance by the capable. But, when one considers the obstacles to achieving the meritocratic ideal, it does look as if a fairer world must be temporarily ordered.
paras.zh: 我理解雷丁的不情愿——也理解她的沮丧。我也不喜欢配额；它们与我信奉的英才制度，即由能者治理，背道而驰。但是，只要想一想实现英才理想的重重障碍，就确实会让人觉得：一个更公平的世界暂时只能靠强制命令来促成。

paras.en: After all, four decades of evidence has now shown that corporations in Europe as well as the US are evading the meritocratic hiring and promotion of women to top positions — no matter how much "soft pressure" is put upon them. When women do break through to the summit of corporate power — as, for example, Sheryl Sandberg recently did at Facebook — they attract massive attention precisely because they remain the exception to the rule.
paras.zh: 毕竟，四十年的证据已经表明：无论施加多少“软压力”，欧洲和美国的公司都在回避按英才原则聘用和提拔女性进入高层。当女性真的突破重围登上企业权力顶峰时——例如谢丽尔·桑德伯格最近在脸书做到的那样——她们会引来大量关注，恰恰因为她们仍是规则之外的例外。

paras.en: If appropriate public policies were in place to help all women — whether CEOs or their children's caregivers — and all families, Sandberg would be no more newsworthy than any other highly capable person living in a more just society.
paras.zh: 如果有恰当的公共政策来帮助所有女性——无论是首席执行官还是她们孩子的看护者——并帮助所有家庭，那么桑德伯格就不会比一个更公正社会里的任何其他高能力者更具新闻价值。

items.stem: In the European corporate workplace, generally
items.exp: 定位第一段 Europe's top corporate-governance positions remain overwhelmingly male，且女性只占董事会 14%，可见决策权在男性手中，B 的 men have the final say 是对“压倒性由男性占据”的口语化改写。A 与 overwhelmingly male 相反；C 把 governance 与 overwhelmed 硬凑，原文的 overwhelmingly 修饰的是 male；D 与 will never be completely family-friendly 直接矛盾。

items.stem: The European Union's intended legislation is
items.exp: 定位第二段 This proposed mandate was born of frustration：雷丁的自愿呼吁只有 24 家公司响应，欧盟才转向强制立法，属不得已之举，C 正确。D 的 voluntary action 说的是去年的呼吁，不是眼下的立法；B 把因果弄反——立法是呼吁失败后的补救，而非对呼吁的“响应”；A 与“性别并不平衡”的现实相反。

items.stem: According to Reding, quotas may help women
items.exp: 定位第四段：配额“open the way to equality and they break through the glass ceiling”，并以法国等“以法律条款把女性送入企业高层”的国家为证，落点就是让女性获得高层职位，A 正确。B 的 see through 是“看穿、看透”，原文 break through 是“打破”，属形近陷阱；C 是第三段提出的问题背景；D 的 legal results 是对 legally binding provisions 的误读。

items.stem: The author's attitude toward Reding's appeal is one of
items.exp: 定位第五段 I understand Reding's reluctance — and her frustration ... it does look as if a fairer world must be temporarily ordered：作者理解并接受了“暂时强制”的必要，态度是赞同，D 正确。A 的怀疑针对的是配额在理念上的瑕疵，作者随即用 But 转折；B 的 objectiveness 过于中性，掩盖了末段 Sandberg would be no more newsworthy 的明显倾向；C 与通篇评论的姿态不符。

items.stem: Women entering top management become headlines due to the lack of
items.exp: 定位末段 If appropriate public policies were in place ... Sandberg would be no more newsworthy than any other highly capable person：她们之所以成为新闻，正是因为缺少恰当的公共政策，C 正确。B 的 massive media attention 是“成为头条”的表现而非原因，属因果倒置；A 的社会公正、D 的软压力是文中另有所指的概念，都答不了 lack of 这一问。

sections.title: Section II Part B　选小标题（为段落匹配标题）
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subtitle from the list A - G for each numbered paragraph (41 - 45). There are two extra subtitles which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：靠救济金过日子的美食博主给出的省钱吃好建议。B“均衡饮食”只在 41 段顺带一提，A“像农民一样生活”与去米其林犒劳自己正相反。
sections.intro: The hugely popular blog the Skint Foodie chronicles how Tony balances his love of good food with living on benefits. After bills, Tony has £ 60 a week to spend, £ 40 of which goes on food, but 10 years ago he was earning £ 130,000 a year working in corporate communications and eating at London's best restaurants at least twice a week. Then his marriage failed, his career burned out and his drinking became serious. "The community mental health team saved my life. And I felt like that again, to a certain degree, when people responded to the blog so well. It gave me the validation and confidence that I'd lost. But it's still a day-by-day thing." Now he's living in a council flat and fielding offers from literary agents. He's feeling positive, but he'll carry on blogging — not about eating as cheaply as you can — "there are so many people in a much worse state, with barely any money to spend on food" — but eating well on a budget. Here's his advice for economical foodies.

blocks.en: Impulsive spending isn't an option, so plan your week's menu in advance, making shopping lists for your ingredients in their exact quantities. I have an Excel template for a week of breakfast, lunch and dinner. Stop laughing: it's not just cost effective but helps you balance your diet. It's also a good idea to shop daily instead of weekly, because, being human, you'll sometimes change your mind about what you fancy.
blocks.zh: 冲动消费是不可能的，所以要提前规划一周的菜单，按精确用量为食材列出购物清单。我有一个涵盖一周早、中、晚餐的 Excel 模板。别笑：它不仅能省钱，还能帮你均衡饮食。另一个好主意是每天而不是每周采购，因为人嘛，有时会改主意，想吃别的。
blocks.exp: 定位本段首句 Impulsive spending isn't an option, so plan your week's menu in advance, making shopping lists for your ingredients in their exact quantities，全段都在讲“提前规划菜单、列清单”，F 的 Planning is everything 正是概括。B 的 Balance your diet 只是段中顺带一提的附带好处（helps you balance your diet），不是段落中心；E 说的是 42 段“按需购买”的内容。

blocks.en: This is where supermarkets and their anonymity come in handy. With them, there's not the same embarrassment as when buying one carrot in a little greengrocer. And if you plan properly, you'll know that you only need, say, 350g of shin of beef and six rashers of bacon, not whatever weight is pre-packed in the supermarket chiller.
blocks.zh: 这正是超市及其“匿名性”派上用场的地方。在超市里，不会像在小蔬菜店里只买一根胡萝卜那样尴尬。而且只要规划得当，你就会知道自己只需要比如 350 克牛腱肉和六片培根，而不是冷藏柜里预先包装好的那个分量。
blocks.exp: 定位本段：you'll know that you only need, say, 350g of shin of beef and six rashers of bacon, not whatever weight is pre-packed——强调按自己的需要买、不被超市的包装分量牵着走，E 的 Stick to what you need 对应。C 的 Shopkeepers are your friends 是 44 段“与肉铺、鱼摊交朋友”的内容，此处提到的超市恰恰是“无人情味”的反面场景。

blocks.en: You may proudly claim to only have frozen peas in the freezer — that's not good enough. Mine is filled with leftovers, bread, stock, meat and fish. Planning ahead should eliminate wastage, but if you have surplus vegetables you'll do a vegetable soup, and all fruits threatening to "go off" will be cooked or juiced.
blocks.zh: 你也许会得意地说，冰箱里只有冷冻豌豆——这还不够。我的冰箱塞满了剩菜、面包、高汤、肉和鱼。提前规划应该能避免浪费；但如果有富余的蔬菜，就做一锅蔬菜汤，所有眼看要“坏掉”的水果都会被煮掉或榨汁。
blocks.exp: 定位本段 Planning ahead should eliminate wastage 以及“剩菜做汤、快坏的水果煮掉或榨汁”的整套做法，通篇讲“不糟蹋东西”，G 的 Waste not, want not（不浪费就不缺）最贴。B 的 Balance your diet 在 41 段出现，A 的 Live like a peasant 与“把冰箱塞满”的丰足感相反，都不合本段。

blocks.en: Everyone says this, but it really is a top tip for frugal eaters. Shop at butchers, delis and fish-sellers regularly, even for small things, and be super friendly. Soon you'll feel comfortable asking if they've any knuckles of ham for soups and stews, or beef bones, chicken carcasses and fish heads for stock which, more often than not, they'll let you have for free.
blocks.zh: 这话人人都说，但对精打细算的吃客来说确实是头等妙招。经常光顾肉铺、熟食店和鱼摊，哪怕只买一点点，并且要格外友好。很快你就能很自然地开口问，他们有没有炖汤炖菜用的猪肘子，或者熬高汤用的牛骨、鸡架和鱼头——这些东西他们多半会白送给你。
blocks.exp: 定位本段 Shop at butchers, delis and fish-sellers regularly ... be super friendly ... they'll let you have for free：与店主混熟就能白拿骨头、鱼头，C 的 Shopkeepers are your friends 正是此意。D 的 Remember to treat yourself 是 45 段“每几个月下馆子犒劳自己”的内容；A 的 peasant 只取“省钱”一端，漏掉了“靠人情”这层关键。

blocks.en: You won't be eating out a lot, but save your pennies and once every few months treat yourself to a set lunch at a good restaurant — £ 1.75 a week for three months gives you £ 21 — more than enough for a three-course lunch at Michelin-starred Arbutus. It's £ 16.95 there — or £ 12.99 for a large pizza from Domino's: I know which I'd rather eat.
blocks.zh: 你不会经常下馆子，但要攒下零钱，每隔几个月到好餐厅犒劳自己一顿套餐午餐——每周省 1.75 英镑，三个月就是 21 英镑，足够在米其林星级餐厅 Arbutus 吃一顿三道菜午餐（那里要 16.95 英镑），或者买一份达美乐的大号披萨（12.99 英镑）：我知道自己更愿意吃哪个。
blocks.exp: 定位本段 save your pennies and once every few months treat yourself to a set lunch at a good restaurant，treat yourself 与 D 逐词对应，也是本段唯一的主张。A 的 Live like a peasant 是把“节省”推到极端，与“去米其林餐厅吃套餐”正相反，是最强的反向干扰；G 的 waste not 属于 43 段的剩菜处理，与“犒劳自己”无关。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 难点：put it to one side 译“搁到一边”，pop into my mind 译“突然浮现”；Hair 是音乐剧名《头发》。

paras.en: I can pick a date from the past 53 years and know instantly where I was, what happened in the news and even the day of the week. I've been able to do this since I was four.
paras.zh: 我能从过去 53 年里随手挑出一个日期，立刻说出当时我在哪里、新闻里发生了什么，甚至连那天是星期几都记得。我从四岁起就有这种本领。

paras.en: I never feel overwhelmed with the amount of information my brain absorbs. My mind seems to be able to cope and the information is stored away neatly. When I think of a sad memory, I do what everybody does - try to put it to one side. I don't think it's harder for me just because my memory is clearer. Powerful memory doesn't make my emotions any more acute or vivid. I can recall the day my grandfather died and the sadness I felt when we went to the hospital the day before. I also remember that the musical play Hair opened on Broadway on the same day — they both just pop into my mind in the same way.
paras.zh: 我从未因为大脑吸收的信息量之大而不堪重负。我的心智似乎应付得来，信息也被井井有条地存放起来。想起伤心往事时，我和所有人一样——尽量把它搁到一边。我不认为因为自己的记忆更清晰，这件事对我而言就更难。强大的记忆力并没有让我的情感变得更强烈、更鲜明。我能回忆起祖父去世那天的情形，以及前一天我们去医院时我的悲伤。我也记得音乐剧《头发》就在同一天于百老汇开演——这两件事就这样以同样的方式突然浮现在我脑海里。

words: 不堪重负的，不知所措的

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（倡议邮件）
sections.dir: Suppose your class is to hold a charity sale for kids in need of help. Write your classmates an email to 1) inform them about the details, and 2) encourage them to participate. (about 100 words)
sections.note: 两要点：先写清时间、地点、卖什么、钱给谁，再明确招募与捐赠方式。只喊“请大家参加”会丢分。署名 Li Ming。
sections.sample:
Dear classmates,

Our class will hold a charity sale for children in need on Saturday, June 15, from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the east gate of the campus. All the money raised will go to the children's hospital, where it will buy books and winter clothes for the young patients.

We need your help. Please bring any idle books, toys, clothes or handicrafts to Room 302 before Friday noon, and sign up to work at one of our stalls for two hours. Even a small donation makes a difference.

I look forward to your support.

Yours,
Li Ming
tips: 开头三句把细节交代完：时间、地点、义卖所得用途，这是第 1 个要点的全部得分点
第 2 个要点要落到“怎么做”——带什么物品到哪里、什么时间前、报名值几小时班，而不是一句 please join us
语气要像同学之间的倡议：we need your help、even a small donation makes a difference，比 I hope you can come 更有号召力
结尾另起一行署名 Li Ming，按要求不写地址、不用真名

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the following chart. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 柱状图四根柱子 67.77%→71.13%→71.93%→88.24%，前三年几乎持平、大四陡升，重点写“为何临近毕业才猛增”。
sections.sample:
The bar chart shows the proportion of students at a certain university who take part-time jobs, grade by grade. The figure edges up from 67.77% for freshmen to 71.13% for sophomores and 71.93% for juniors, and then leaps to 88.24% for seniors.

Two factors may account for this pattern. First, as students move up, spending on textbooks, materials and social activities grows, so many of them need income of their own. Second, the closer graduation comes, the more anxious students become about their resumes; part-time work offers the practical experience that employers value, and a senior has only a few months left to gain it. That is why the curve stays almost flat for three years and then shoots up in the final one.

In my view, such experience is worth having, but it should not come at the cost of study. Students should choose jobs related to their major, keep working hours within limits, and remember that a solid academic record is still the foundation of any career.
tips: 第一段只读数并点出“三年平、一年陡”的形态：67.77%、71.13%、71.93% 三个数可以并成一句，88.24% 单独强调，别四根柱子平均用力
第二段解释陡升：学费与社交开支增加＋求职竞争需要简历，两条原因都要落到“为什么是大四”这一点上
第三段表态要有限度：赞成积累经验，但给出可执行的边界（与专业相关、限工时、学业为本），避免写成一边倒的赞美
